title: Komodo dragons
text:
The Komodo dragon is the largest lizard in the world. In the wild, it lives only on a few islands in Indonesia, including Komodo, Rinca and Flores.

What they look like
An adult Komodo dragon can grow up to three metres long and can weigh as much as a grown-up person. It has rough, scaly skin, strong legs and sharp, curved claws. Its long yellow tongue is forked at the end.

Hunting and eating
Komodo dragons are meat eaters. They hunt deer and wild pigs, and they also eat animals that are already dead. A dragon flicks its tongue in and out to pick up smells from the air. This helps it find food that is several kilometres away. After a very big meal, a dragon may not need to eat again for weeks.

Young dragons
A female lays her eggs in a nest in the ground. When the babies hatch, they climb up into the trees. Living in the branches keeps them safe from bigger dragons. Up there, they eat insects, eggs and small lizards.

Protecting dragons
There are only a few thousand Komodo dragons left in the wild. Komodo National Park was set up in 1980 to protect them and the other animals that share their islands. Visitors can see the dragons, but only with a trained ranger, because the dragons are wild animals and can be dangerous.
